mainEntity.name: Can I use my existing Claude and Codex subscriptions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You log each agent CLI into your own plan once on the server, and Manta runs them side by side. No Manta account, no proxy, no per-seat fee.

mainEntity.name: How long does setup actually take?

acceptedAnswer.text: About two minutes. Point the desktop app at a server and it installs the runtime, starts the service, gets a certificate and shows a six-digit pairing code for your other devices.

mainEntity.name: Does the agent keep running if I close my laptop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Agents live in tmux sessions on the box as system services. Clients are disposable; close them all and the work continues, with full history when you reconnect.

mainEntity.name: What kind of server do I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any always-on Linux box or Apple Silicon Mac. A five dollar VPS is enough. The installer touches no system packages and brings its own runtime.

mainEntity.name: Does my code leave my box?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Transcripts, uploads, secrets and config stay on the machine. The only outbound traffic is your agent talking to its own provider.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Tailscale, a VPN or port forwarding?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If Tailscale is already running, devices connect over your tailnet. If not, the box gets its own hostname and certificate. Either way, nothing to port-forward.

mainEntity.name: Is Manta really open source?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes: MIT licensed, client and server both. Read every line, build it yourself, run it with no connection to us. No account, no hosted tier. Telemetry is optional and sends nothing unless you set a token.

mainEntity.name: Is this an alternative to Conductor or Orca?

acceptedAnswer.text: They overlap on a different bet. Those run agents on your Mac; Manta runs them on a server you own and gives every device the same window onto the work.

claude-code-mobile.html.title: Claude Code on mobile: full parity iPhone
claude-code-mobile.html.description: Run Claude Code from your phone with full transcript, live tool output, dictation and one-tap approvals.

mainEntity.name: Is the phone app a viewer or a real client?

acceptedAnswer.text: A real client. The iPhone app is a native app that talks straight to the same box as the desktop. You get the full transcript, live tool output, approvals, dictation and file upload, not a status page that links out to your laptop.

mainEntity.name: Is there a version for Android or other phones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not yet. The phone client is a native iPhone app; there is no browser client. The desktop app covers macOS and Windows, and your agents run on any Linux box or Mac you own. The remote page covers running the agents on a box.

mainEntity.name: Do notifications wake up the phone even when I am at my desk?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Manta's push routing only sends to the phone when the desktop is not foreground or active. At your desk, the desktop rings. Away from it, the phone rings. Blocking asks like a permission request ring every device at once, because the agent is stuck until you answer.

mainEntity.name: Can I dictate a reply instead of typing on the phone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Hold the mic, speak, release, and the transcript lands in the composer ready to send or edit.

mainEntity.name: Does the phone talk to my laptop or straight to the box?

acceptedAnswer.text: Straight to the box. The phone pairs with the box directly over HTTPS, the same way the desktop does. Your laptop does not need to be open. Closing the laptop does not drop the phone.

claude-code-remote.html.title: Claude Code remote: run it on a server you own
claude-code-remote.html.description: Run Claude Code on a VPS or home server. Real tmux, push notifications, and the work outlives the laptop.

mainEntity.name: Can I run Claude Code on a VPS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The installer runs on Debian, Ubuntu and the usual Linux suspects, with Caddy and a Let's Encrypt certificate when you need public ingress. The agent runs in a real tmux session on the box, so it outlives every device that connects to it.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to forward a port?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If Tailscale is already running on the box, devices connect over your tailnet and nothing is published to the internet. If Tailscale is not running, the installer provisions a hostname and a certificate, which is the only public surface. You never forward a port by hand.

mainEntity.name: What happens when I close my laptop?

acceptedAnswer.text: The agent keeps running, because it lives in a tmux session on the box. The box is a system service. When you pair your phone again, the same session is there with the full history. The mobile page covers what the phone sees when this happens.

mainEntity.name: Does this work without a public DNS record?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Pick the tailnet path at install time and the box has no public DNS, no certificate, and no open port. Devices reach it over your tailnet at a private IPv4.

mainEntity.name: Is this self-hosted Claude Code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and the install script is auditable before you pipe it into bash. The repository is MIT licensed and the server runs on hardware you control. The open source page covers what that means in practice.

open-source.html.title: Manta is open source and self-hosted
open-source.html.description: Manta is MIT licensed, self-hosted, and has no account and no seat count.

mainEntity.name: Where is the source code?

acceptedAnswer.text: On GitHub at github.com/antoinedc/MantaUI. The server, the Electron desktop app, the React renderer, the phone client and the install script all live in the same repository.

mainEntity.name: What is the licence?

acceptedAnswer.text: MIT. The full text is in the LICENSE file at the root of the repository. It is permissive: fork it, modify it, ship a derivative, keep the copyright notice.

mainEntity.name: What stays on my box?

acceptedAnswer.text: Everything. Transcripts, uploads, secrets, configuration, schedules, peer metadata, ingress choice. The only outbound traffic is your agent talking to its model provider, and a small push payload carrying the session name when you turn on phone notifications.

mainEntity.name: Can I run my own gateway or push provider?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fork the repo, point the push routing at your own gateway, edit the manifest. The push and webhook modules are designed to be replaced. The same goes for the install script, the installer, and the desktop app.

mainEntity.name: Does the box phone home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only to your model provider and to APNs, when you have phone notifications turned on. Telemetry is an optional, token-gated log-shipper — nothing leaves the box unless you set a token. The pricing page covers what you actually pay for.

pricing.html.title: Manta pricing: free, MIT, self-hosted
pricing.html.description: Manta is free and open source. You pay your model provider and supply the box. There are no tiers and no seat count.

mainEntity.name: Is Manta really free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The server, the desktop client, the phone client and the install script are MIT licensed and free. There is no paid tier and no per-seat fee. A native iPhone app is planned, but the server you self-host stays free. You pay your model provider and you supply the box.

mainEntity.name: What does it cost to run?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whatever you spend on the model and whatever you spend on the box. A $5 VPS is enough to host a single agent for a single user. Most teams reuse hardware they already have, which means the marginal cost is the model spend.

mainEntity.name: Will there be paid tiers in the future?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The product is the binary on GitHub. Anything that lands in main lands in your box when you update. There is no paid feature in the roadmap, and there are no plans to add one.

mainEntity.name: Does Manta take a cut of my API spend?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Manta does not bill you, does not see your API spend, and does not sit between you and your model provider. You give the agent your key, the agent talks to the provider directly, and the bill comes from the provider.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I stop paying for the box?

acceptedAnswer.text: The server stops. The data is plain text on the disk, so a reinstall on a new box picks up where the old one left off, and a permanent shutdown is just an uninstall. There is nothing to migrate off and no vendor to call. The open source page covers the part that makes this possible.

vs-orca.html.title: Manta UI vs Orca: an honest comparison
vs-orca.html.description: A fair side-by-side of Manta UI and Orca (onorca.dev) on architecture, mobile, remote access, permissions, diff review, agent runtimes, and licensing.

mainEntity.name: Is Manta a fork of Orca?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. They are separate products with separate codebases. Both are MIT, both run Claude Code in a terminal, and the similarity ends there. Orca is desktop-first and ships 34 agent runtimes; Manta is box-first and ships a handful of CLI runtimes.

mainEntity.name: Does Manta run on any of Orca's agent runtimes?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Manta runs Claude Code, Codex, Kimi and opencode in real tmux sessions on your box. Orca's runtime count comes from packaging many agent CLIs into the desktop app; Manta does not do that today and would not benefit from the same approach because it does not own the editor.

mainEntity.name: Can Manta and Orca share a machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, on a macOS box. They use different ports and different tmux sessions, so they do not interfere. On a Linux box the same applies; the desktop piece of Orca simply has no Linux desktop binary to launch there.

mainEntity.name: Why is Orca so much more mature?

acceptedAnswer.text: Orca is older, has 29.6k stars on GitHub, and is YC-backed. Manta is a solo project and is younger. Maturity buys you a larger surface today (diff review, an editor, more runtimes, a Linux desktop) and a smaller backlog. We concede the comparison on maturity plainly.

mainEntity.name: Which one should I pick if my work runs locally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Orca. Manta is for when the work needs to outlive the laptop, or when you want a phone client that can approve a command. If neither matters and your editor matters most, Orca's Monaco integration is the answer.

vs-conductor.html.title: Manta UI vs Conductor: an honest comparison
vs-conductor.html.description: A fair side-by-side of Manta UI and Conductor (conductor.build) on architecture, platforms, sandboxing, diff review, the paid Cloud beta, and licensing.

mainEntity.name: Is Manta a fork of Conductor?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. They are separate products from separate teams. Manta is MIT and solo. Conductor is closed source, YC S24, and has raised $24M. Both run Claude Code in a chat panel.

mainEntity.name: Why is Conductor macOS only?

acceptedAnswer.text: Per Conductor's own docs: not available for Windows or Linux yet. conductor.build/docs Manta's box runs on Linux or macOS today, which is the path to running agents on a server.

mainEntity.name: Does Conductor's "Cloud" beta do what Manta does?

acceptedAnswer.text: It tries to, with restrictions. Conductor Cloud is in beta, requires the Pro tier, supports GitHub only, and caps you at 10 workspaces. Manta runs on your own box, is free, supports any agent runtime that ships a CLI, and has no workspace cap.

mainEntity.name: Is Conductor more secure than Manta?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and Conductor says so itself: Agents run directly on your system without sandboxing and Workspace isolation is development isolation, not a security boundary. conductor.build/docs/security Manta's default is that every command shows up as a permission card you answer.

mainEntity.name: Which one should I pick if I edit heavily and run on macOS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Conductor. Its Mac-native editor, diff review with inline comments back to the agent, and Linear/GitHub depth are the strongest parts of its product. Manta is for when the work has to outlive the laptop, or when you want a phone client.

vs-ssh-tmux.html.title: Manta UI vs Termius + SSH: an honest comparison
vs-ssh-tmux.html.description: A fair side-by-side of Manta UI and the incumbent Termius-over-SSH stack for running Claude Code on your own VPS.

itemListElement.name: Manta UI vs SSH and tmux

mainEntity.name: Does Manta replace SSH?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. SSH still works on the same box. You can ssh into the box, attach to the same tmux session Manta is steering, and continue from the terminal.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to give up Termius?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Termius keeps connecting to the same box. The chat panel and the phone client are the parts that change. Most people we expect to talk to run both: Termius for editor-heavy work, Manta for chat and phone.

mainEntity.name: Does Manta work alongside Claude Code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Manta runs Claude Code in a tmux session on the box. The same session can be attached from Termius or steered from Manta's chat panel. The model provider stays the same.

mainEntity.name: Will Manta's installer break my existing SSH setup?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The installer adds a system service (manta-server) and either opens no public port (Tailscale path) or one HTTPS port (Caddy + LE on a per-box hostname). It does not change your SSH config, your authorized keys, or your sshd settings.

mainEntity.name: Should I add Manta or stick with my current setup?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your current setup covers your needs, keep it. Manta is for the cases SSH does not cover: a phone app that can actually approve a command, a notification when the agent gets stuck, dictation, file upload, and tools the agent can use between turns.
